hook: Sam Altman has been chief executive of OpenAI since 2019 and was president of Y Combinator for the five years before that. He studied computer science at Stanford and left after two years, founding the location-sharing app Loopt in 2005, which became one of the first companies Y Combinator funded and was acquired by Green Dot in 2012 for 43 million dollars. He returned to Y Combinator as a partner, then ran it from 2014 to 2019, a period in which it backed roughly 1,900 companies including Airbnb, DoorDash, Instacart, Reddit and Twitch. OpenAI was founded in 2015 as a nonprofit with Altman and Elon Musk as co-chairs; the structure that grew out of it, a for-profit arm controlled by a nonprofit board, is the arrangement that later produced both the Microsoft partnership and the governance crisis that briefly removed him.
name: Sam Altman

quote.text: How to make decisions with very imperfect information.
quote.context: Sam Altman on what poker taught him, to The New York Times, 2023

reading.body:
Sam Altman is the single figure most responsible for moving generative AI from a research context into mass public use and onto legislative agendas, doing both within roughly six months in 2022 and 2023.

The ChatGPT launch in November 2022 reached an estimated hundred million users in two months, a speed of adoption that had no prior consumer-product equivalent in the data. That scale of deployment created the demand signal that now pulls on compute, data-center construction, and grid capacity across the industry. The GPT APIs extended that pressure downstream, making frontier models the substrate for thousands of businesses and multiplying the number of organizations with a direct stake in AI infrastructure.

The Senate testimony and the November 2023 board crisis belong to a different register. Altman asking Congress for licensing and safety standards opened regulation as a mainstream legislative project, and his firing and reinstatement within five days exposed how fragile governance-by-charter can be at organizations where the stakes are this high. The data covers his leadership role, his public-facing moments, and the broad shape of the developer ecosystem he helped build. It does not cover OpenAI's compute agreements, power procurement, or capital structure, so the direct line from his decisions to specific infrastructure outcomes is not something this record establishes.

timeline.event: OpenAI founded as a nonprofit with Altman and Elon Musk as co-chairs
timeline.impact: Framed as developing AI for the benefit of humanity, with a billion dollars in committed funding

quick_facts: CEO of OpenAI since 2019, and a co-chair of the organisation from its founding in 2015
President of Y Combinator from 2014 to 2019, succeeding Paul Graham
Founded Loopt in 2005, one of the first Y Combinator companies; acquired by Green Dot in 2012 for 43 million dollars
Co-founded the venture fund Hydrazine Capital with his brother Max in 2012
Studied computer science at Stanford and left after two years
OpenAI launched with a billion dollars in funding from Altman, Musk, Peter Thiel and Amazon Web Services among others
Removed as CEO by OpenAI's board on 17 November 2023 and reinstated on 21 November after most employees threatened to resign
Born 22 April 1985 in Chicago and raised in the suburbs of St. Louis

achievements.title: ChatGPT
achievements.impact: Released in late 2022 and reaching more than a million users within five days, it brought large language models to public attention and set off the policy response that followed, including a US executive order and the UK AI Safety Summit.

achievements.title: OpenAI
achievements.impact: Co-chaired at its 2015 founding as a nonprofit and has led as CEO since 2019, through the creation of the for-profit arm, the Microsoft partnership and the GPT and DALL-E product lines.

achievements.title: Y Combinator
achievements.impact: Ran the accelerator from 2014 to 2019, during which it backed roughly 1,900 companies and established the twice-yearly cohort model as the template for startup accelerators.

achievements.title: Loopt
achievements.impact: Founded in 2005 after leaving Stanford, an early location-sharing app that attracted carrier partnerships but not users, and was acquired for 43 million dollars in 2012.

achievements.title: Surviving the 2023 board crisis
achievements.impact: Fired on 17 November 2023 over candour with the board and reinstated four days later after nearly all OpenAI employees signed a letter demanding the board resign. The episode reshaped the company's governance and became the clearest public test of whether a nonprofit board could control a frontier lab.
